title: debark install report v1
description: debark.installreport/v1 - the machine-readable result of `debark install --json` (also used for --status and --dry-run, where applied is false). Never written into a bundle; a wire/API response object. install never proceeds without a verify report; this schema mirrors verifyreport.v1.schema.json's Report shape locally under $defs/VerifyReport so this document can be validated standalone.

started_at.description: When this run started, RFC 3339 UTC, second precision.

finished_at.description: When this run finished. Absent for a report still in progress.

bundle_path.description: Path to the bundle being installed.

verify.description: The verification report; install never proceeds without one.

applied.description: False for Plan, --status and --dry-run; true once changes were actually made.

ok.description: True when the requested state was reached.

to_install.description: Packages apt would install or did install, name=version form, parsed from apt's simulation.

to_upgrade.description: Packages apt would upgrade or did upgrade, name=version form.

to_remove.description: Packages apt would remove or did remove, name=version form.

already_current.description: Count of bundle packages the target already has at the locked version.

target_expected.description: The target identity the lock was built for.

target_actual.description: The target identity actually found on this machine.

base_divergence.description: How far this machine differs from the base a synthesized bundle assumed. Absent for the ordinary case of a bundle built from a captured snapshot, which is a measurement of this machine and so has no assumption to diverge from.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes: codename mismatch, dpkg fallback used, holds bypassed.

apt_output_digest.description: SHA-256 of the captured apt output, kept in the local evidence log.

BaseDivergence.description: Present only when the bundle's snapshot.json says origin.kind is "synthesized" (ADR-014). A synthesized snapshot asserts what a stock install of a release contains; install is the one place that assertion can be checked against a real dpkg status. A package the base assumed and the machine lacks means the bundle may be SHORT, which is the failure debark exists to prevent - but it is a finding, reported as a warning, and never a refusal.

base_id.description: The base definition the bundle was built against, e.g. "ubuntu:26.04/desktop"; restated from the snapshot's origin.base_id.

assumed.description: How many distinct packages the base claimed a stock install already has - the size of the assumption, and the denominator for missing.

missing.description: Every assumed package, name:arch, that dpkg does not report as installed on this machine, sorted. The complete list; the human warning names only a bounded sample. The opposite direction (packages present but not assumed) is deliberately not recorded: it makes the bundle larger than it needed to be, which is harmless.

checked_at.description: When this check ran, RFC 3339 UTC, second precision.

bundle_path.description: Path to the bundle that was checked.

bundle_id.description: The manifest's bundle_id, when it could be parsed.

ok.description: True only when every check passed.

signed.description: Whether the bundle carried at least one signature block.

signatures.description: Outcome of checking each signature block present.

files_checked.description: Number of files whose digest was verified.

bytes_checked.description: Total bytes read while verifying file digests.

target.description: Target identity restated from the manifest.

signer_kind.description: Which Signer implementation produced this block.

key_id.description: Identifies the key this block claims to be signed by.

valid.description: True when the signature verified cryptographically against a trusted key.

trusted.description: False when cryptographically valid but signed by an untrusted key.

detail.description: Extra explanation, when there is one.

path.description: The file this problem is about, when it is about one file.

expected.description: Expected digest or size, rendered as a string.

got.description: Actual digest or size found, rendered as a string.
